decision: Qualify TQP-55 and TQP-56, promote TQP-57 as the first limited Windows CPU reference production release, close Gate F, and advance the dependency-ordered program to TQP-58 without widening the release beyond its evidence.
evidence: world-transvoxel-terrain commit 20f0a6e4b5fd32016e106a1bac9c1248f2d2a81f and addon tree bd8b7c6ebde90c483ff354f97db09512008e6fcc
world-transvoxel-integration-game commit efadb8dd900056e2d7f8696685605281beafb36b repins and passes TQP-54 on Godot 4.7
TQP-56 60.2-second wrapper run with 80 cycles 20 edits 26 queries 6 restarts about 1 MB memory growth and zero queue rejections plus retained 1802.58-second TQP-49 evidence
qualified_scope: Windows x86-64 Godot 4.7 Forward+ CPU Terrain Standard 1.0 reference matrix
standalone world-transvoxel-terrain 1.0.0 addon with exact external world-transvoxel authority
bounded production-wrapper and retained long-run evidence
unqualified_scope: non-Windows arbitrary hardware GPU terrain complete-system power gameplay networking and universal 16 W 60 FPS claims
standards_changed: TQP-55 through TQP-57 production standards and retained evidence
Gate F promotion and TQP-58 next milestone
review: The release is authoritative only inside the pinned matrix. TQP-48 target misses remain explicit; the release does not convert reference ceilings into universal guarantees.
downstream_impact: The CPU production release becomes the differential baseline for TQP-58 through TQP-64. GPU work may improve measured behavior but cannot silently rewrite CPU authority or its retained evidence.
